svg.title: Framework: agentic iterative dexterous sim-to-real learning
svg.desc: Stage 1, Demo-to-Sim: task inputs and standardized reference assets feed an AI research agent that understands the task, builds a training simulator, designs rewards, selects a training strategy and learns an initial policy. Stage 2, Iterative Sim-to-Target Learning: a closed loop of executing the policy in the target environment, retrieving sensor-based target feedback, comparing target and training simulator, diagnosing failures, improving simulator, training strategy or policy, evaluating candidates and repeating. A replay alignment mechanism (target rollout, fixed-action replay in the training simulator, trajectory divergence analysis, simulator calibration, policy improvement) interleaves calibration and policy optimization. Human-defined and fixed: task success criteria, target evaluation rules, hardware and safety constraints. Agent-defined and improvable: training reward, simulator, learning method, policy. Objectives per task: object or motion tracking, task success rate, or task throughput. Dashed elements are planned and not part of the current experiment.

g.text: build an initial simulator and policy from task references
task reference, not a motion target
same asset types and interface for every task

text.tspan: Every field carries a status — observed, estimated or
unobservable — so missing data is explicit, never silent.

g.text: agent selects which references to use
closed-loop research: the agent improves simulator, training strategy and policy from target feedback
set before research; the agent cannot change them
proposed, tested and revised by the agent every iteration
The training reward is distinct from the fixed task success criteria.
human-motion similarity is optional, never required
planned (not yet in the current experiment)

svg.text: Privileged ground-truth object states are never inputs to the agent; all target feedback is estimated from sensors and logs.
